declarations.objective: Map a domain model against the knowledge a repository already holds, returning a closed verdict of none, update, or create and one entry per implicated artifact with the operation it takes, the reason, and the model element driving it. Choose it once a domain model exists and before any knowledge object is authored. Not for modelling, not for classifying constructs into node types, not for authoring, and not for judging whether the change is a good idea.

required_context.note: Classification reads what a change touches, not the whole ontology. A lifecycle, an interface, and a process are reached through the objects above rather than selected directly, so naming all six would narrow nothing.

deterministic_behavior: the domain model is validated against domain-model/4 at the boundary before it is analysed, and a blocked model ends the run
base_state records whether anything existed to implicate, observed rather than inferred
over an empty base the verdict is create and every entry names a domain model element
entries are sorted by identifier, so two analyses of one model compare directly
judgment: which knowledge objects a request semantically implicates
whether the implication amounts to none, an update, or a creation

grant.note: Read-only on purpose. A judgement that could also edit what it judges is not a judgement, and the boundary validator is not this agent's to run.

failure_outcomes.reason: a required input was not supplied, named in the result rather than substituted
an identifier the analysis would name does not resolve in the graph
the request asks for two things that cannot both hold, named so a caller can decide

declarations.objective: Analyse a request into a DDD domain model — subdomains, bounded contexts and their relationships, aggregates, entities and value objects, invariants, lifecycles, published interfaces, and processes — marking every element as stated by the request or decided by the analysis. Choose it when a request describes a problem or a solution and no domain model exists. Not for classifying a model into the ontology, which is domain-analyst; not for authoring knowledge objects; and not for deciding anything about a technology stack.

inputs.name: referenced_material
inputs.default: absent, and the analysis rests on the request alone rather than on material nothing supplied

required_context.note: No node type is in scope. This capability works in DDD's vocabulary and produces a design; the ontology's six types enter one step later, when the model is classified. Naming a node type here would put classification in two capabilities.

deterministic_behavior: the request is received as prose and its identifier as a value; nothing about it is inferred
the result is validated against domain-model/4 at the boundary before anything consumes it
the state is one of the closed set modeled, blocked, and no other value is accepted
every element declares origin as stated or modeled, and an element it decided carries the rationale that decided it
the model id comes from the caller and is never minted

an element whose origin is unclear is recorded as modeled rather than stated, which is the stricter reading: it demands a rationale and invites review, where a wrong `stated` would claim the request said something it did not
judgment: the whole of the modelling: subdomain classification, context boundaries, aggregate boundaries, which constructs are entities and which are value objects, and which rules are invariants
what the request leaves undecided, which is recorded as an open question rather than filled
what falls outside domain knowledge and is recorded as excluded

grant.note: Read-only on purpose. It produces a design and writes nothing, so the design is reviewable before the knowledge base changes; the boundary validator is not this agent's to run.

failure_outcomes.reason: a required input was not supplied, including the model id it never mints, named rather than substituted
the request describes no domain to model, reported as blocked rather than modelled into something plausible
a fact the request does not settle, recorded as an open question with what the answer would change; the model still returns and this is not a stop

declarations.objective: Classify a domain model into the ontology, returning one entry per construct with its node type, its DDD value, the identifier it will take, and every required fact the model does not supply. Choose it once a domain model exists and before anything is authored. Not for modelling the domain, which is domain-modeler; not for authoring objects; and not for filling a gap the model leaves.

inputs.name: existing_boundaries
inputs.default: absent, and every boundary in the plan is then a new one rather than silently reusing an identifier nothing confirmed

required_context.note: Classification may land a construct in any of the six, so narrowing this would narrow what may be decided. It is the same reason root-selector names all six, arrived at from the opposite direction: that capability chooses among existing objects and this one decides what an object will be.

deterministic_behavior: the domain model is validated against domain-model/4 at the boundary before it is read
the result is validated against knowledge-intake-plan/6 at the boundary before anything consumes it
the state is one of the closed set classified, blocked, and no other value is accepted
every proposed identifier is computed from the node type and the boundary by the ontology's arithmetic rather than allocated
entries are sorted by proposed identifier, so two classifications of one model compare directly
the intake id comes from the caller and is never minted
a construct whose node type is genuinely ambiguous is classified as the model supports and the alternative is recorded, never resolved silently
judgment: which node type each DDD construct becomes, and the ddd value it carries
which boundary a construct belongs to, and therefore the identifier it takes
whether a construct has a home in the mapping at all, or is stack knowledge or rationale

grant.note: Read-only on purpose. It decides what each construct becomes and writes nothing, so the classification is reviewable before the base changes; the boundary validator is not this agent's to run.

failure_outcomes.reason: a required input was not supplied, including the intake id it never mints, named rather than substituted
the domain model declares itself blocked, so there is no design to classify; reported rather than classified into nothing
a construct the mapping has no home for, recorded on its own entry as `unmapped` rather than forced into a node type; the plan is still classified and the run still finished

a construct the model states in a form the ontology rejects rather than one it leaves incomplete — an attribute typed outside the closed primitive vocabulary is the standing case. Recorded on its own entry as `refused` with the reason, and nothing is authored from it; a missing fact would have been a gap instead

deprecation.reason: The classification it performs is a closed table and identifier arithmetic, and a measured run put the cost at 75,329 tokens for a mapping that was 1:1 with the model in every one of 24 entries. `expand-model` performs the same mapping as a function: same input, same tree, every run, at no token cost — and it writes the objects too, which this agent was read-only to avoid doing. A consumer delegating to this agent still gets a conforming plan; what it does not get is a result two runs can be compared byte for byte.

declarations.objective: Author or revise one knowledge object from the entry a validated classification names, in one of the six node types, conforming to the ontology contract. Choose it at authoring, once a classification exists. Not for deciding which node type a construct becomes, which is domain-analyst, and not for changing the ontology itself.

required_context.note: It may author any of the six, and it must read the neighbours a new object declares edges to, so the whole vocabulary is genuinely in scope.

deterministic_behavior: the result is validated against knowledge-authoring-result/2 at the boundary
the object is validated against knowledge-object/5, including the per-type required fields
the node type and the subject are read from the entry the classification names, never decided again
the timestamp and producer identity come from the caller and are never minted
a fact that would need two node types is reported as blocked rather than compressed into one, because refusing is available here and choosing would author a construct nobody described
judgment: the wording of the object's own body, and what belongs out of scope
whether the entry supplies enough for the node type it names, which is a blocking outcome rather than an invention

grant.note: Write tools to change exactly one object and no shell: the boundary validator runs after it returns, and a guarantee a producer self-reports is not a guarantee.

failure_outcomes.reason: a required input was not supplied, including the instant and producer identity it never mints
the classification holds no entry for the proposed id, named rather than guessed at
an existing object already records this fact, named so the caller decides whether to revise it
the entry is short of a fact its node type requires, named with the field; the object is not authored around it
the entry asks for a fact the classification does not supply, named so a caller can decide

declarations.objective: Turn a request into a reviewable staging tree: analyse it into a DDD domain model, map what that touches in the base, and expand it into one staged knowledge object per construct — then stop for a person to read the diff. Choose it when a request describes a problem or a solution and no staging tree exists for it. Not for enriching or promoting those objects, which is ingest-domain over the tree this produces.

inputs.name: referenced_material
inputs.default: absent, and the analysis rests on the request alone rather than on material nobody supplied

required_context.note: No node type is in scope. This procedure produces a design in DDD's vocabulary; the ontology's six types enter when the model is classified, which is a different entry point.

deterministic_behavior: the model is validated against domain-model/4 at the boundary and rejected rather than repaired
a model whose state is blocked ends the run with the reason reported and nothing expanded
an impact analysis runs for every request before anything is written, including the first against an empty base, and a verdict of none ends the run
the expansion is a script rather than a delegation: the mapping is a closed table and the identifiers are arithmetic, so two runs over one model produce the same tree byte for byte
no file under the knowledge root is written: every file lands in the staging root, and a staged object declares a different contract from the base's until it is promoted
the four fields only judgment supplies are recorded as authoring gaps rather than guessed at, and the next entry point writes them
every gap is checked against what its node type actually requires before the run ends
the run ends with the tree unenriched and unpromoted: the review is a person reading its diff, and a procedure that ends has stopped where one that says so in the middle has not
every identifier and the instant come from the caller and are never minted
judgment: how to phrase the delegation to the modelling agent
what to draw a reviewer's attention to, which is the decided elements, the refusals and the open domain gaps rather than a count
whether a verdict of none is worth overriding, which is the caller's call to take

grant.note: The skill states no allowed-tools, so it runs under the session's grant, recorded rather than implied. It is not model-invocable: it may write the model it produces.

failure_outcomes.reason: a required input was not supplied, including the three identifiers it never mints
the analysis returned blocked because the request describes no domain; a finished run with a negative result rather than an error
the analysis failed its own contract at the boundary, reported with what failed and rejected rather than repaired
the impact analysis returns none: the base already holds what the model describes, so nothing is staged and the diff a reviewer would read would be noise around nothing
the model states something the ontology rejects, named per construct; the remaining constructs still expand, and this is a defect in the model rather than a fact the domain owes

declarations.objective: Turn a reviewed domain model into a knowledge base in two passes with a review between them: expand the model into staged objects deterministically, stop for a person to read the diff, enrich every object in parallel, check that the enrichment stayed inside its fields, and promote. Choose it once a domain model exists and has been reviewed, including the first time a repository is brought under Siegard. Not for modelling the domain, which is model-domain; not for changing one recorded fact; and not for generating code.

inputs.name: system_defaults
inputs.default: absent, and the ingestion stops rather than choosing a timezone, a currency, an identity strategy, or a body-line ceiling the framework has no basis to choose

required_context.note: Ingestion authors into any of the six and orders the authoring by node type, so the whole vocabulary is in scope as a sequence rather than as a selection.

deterministic_behavior: it begins where the review ended: the staging tree already exists, and nothing here produces one
nothing is written under the knowledge root until promotion, and a staged object declares a different contract from the base's until then

a fact the model does not state is recorded as a gap on the object rather than authored around, and an open question the analysis refused to decide is carried rather than answered: a question answered by whoever happened to run this is a domain fact invented by the framework
every object exists before any is enriched, so the enrichments are independent and none is ordered behind another
each enrichment result is read at the boundary to tell an enriched object from a blocked one, and a blocked one is recorded rather than retried
a finding an enricher reports is relayed to the reviewer and never acted on here: the pass that could have edited the design has already finished, and this one may not
the enrichment check runs before promotion, and it is the only thing enforcing which fields the enrichment may touch — a tool grant names tools, not the keys of a file

promotion validates every object against knowledge-object/5 and writes nothing while any is refused; an object with an open domain gap is refused unless the caller asks otherwise, and the request is reported rather than defaulted
the timestamp, the producer identity, and every identifier come from the caller and are never minted

the checks a per-file schema cannot express are reported as owed rather than run: the distribution ships nothing that performs them, and an improvised one would differ between two runs over the same base
judgment: how to phrase each enrichment delegation
what to draw the reviewer's attention to in the staging diff, which is the refused constructs and the open domain gaps rather than a count
whether to promote objects whose domain gaps are open, which is the caller's call to take

grant.note: The skill states no allowed-tools, so it runs under the session's grant, recorded rather than implied. It is not model-invocable: it writes a knowledge base.

failure_outcomes.reason: a required input was not supplied, including the system defaults it never chooses and the identifiers it never mints
the staging root holds no staged object: `/model-domain` has not run for this request, or its tree was already promoted
an enricher could not write the four fields because the material does not support them, named with what was missing; the object stays staged and unenriched
the enrichment changed something the expansion owns, named per object and per field; nothing is promoted and the change is reported rather than reverted
one or more objects fail the base's contract or still owe the domain a fact; nothing is promoted and the staging tree is left intact

declarations.objective: Turn a validated domain model into one staged knowledge object per classified construct and the plan that records what became of every construct. Choose it once a domain model exists and has been reviewed, in place of delegating the classification: the mapping from a DDD construct to a node type is a closed table and the identifiers are arithmetic, so nothing here needs judgment. Not for modelling the domain, and not for writing the four fields only judgment supplies — it records those as gaps and writes nothing under the knowledge root.

required_context.note: It expands into any of the six, so the whole vocabulary is in scope. Unlike the agent it replaces, it selects nothing: the node type follows from the construct's kind by the ontology's own table.

deterministic_behavior: the domain model is validated against domain-model/4 before anything is written, and a model declaring itself blocked ends the run
every construct in the model takes exactly one entry, whose outcome is classified, unmapped, or refused, so what happened to each is answerable in one place and the count checks against the input
each identifier is computed from the node type and the boundary by the ontology's arithmetic, never allocated, so the same model yields the same identifiers on every run
a fact the node type requires and the model does not state becomes a gap on the object, named with what the domain would have to say, and the object is still written

a fact the model states in a form the ontology rejects — an attribute typed outside the closed primitive vocabulary, a reference resolving to no element or to two — refuses that construct, and no file is written for it
the whole run is a function of the model and the caller's stamp: two runs over one model produce byte-identical trees
nothing is written under the knowledge root; every file lands in the staging root the caller names
the intake id, the producer identity, and the instant come from the caller and are never minted

grant.note: No tool grant: it is a script the caller runs, not a component the harness delegates to. It reads the model it is given and writes under the staging root it is given, and reaches neither the knowledge root nor anything else.

failure_outcomes.reason: the model file is absent or the arguments make no sense; exit 2, distinguished from a check that ran and found a problem
the model declares a version this does not read, named rather than coerced
the model declares itself blocked, so there is no design to expand; reported with its reason and nothing written
a construct the model states in a form the ontology rejects, recorded on its own entry with the reason and no file written; the remaining constructs still expand and this is not a stop

declarations.objective: Hold the enrichment pass to the four fields and the body it owns, by re-deriving what the expansion wrote and comparing. Choose it after enrichment and before promotion. It is the only thing enforcing that restriction: a tool grant names tools, not the keys of a file, so `Edit` confined to four fields is prose until something checks it. Not for validating an object against its contract, which is a boundary check, and not for judging what the enrichment wrote.

required_context.note: No node type is in scope. It compares two renderings of the same objects and reads nothing about what they mean.

deterministic_behavior: what the expansion wrote is re-derived from the model rather than read from a stored baseline: the expansion is a function, so a recorded copy would be a second artifact to keep in step
a field the expansion owns that differs is reported, and the ownership line is read from the one module that declares it rather than restated here
a `kind: domain` gap that was removed is reported: only whoever knows the domain closes one
a field written whose `authoring` gap is still open is reported, because closing the gap is what records that the field was filled
a body heading added, removed, or renamed is reported; the content under a heading is not read
an object present in the tree and absent from the expansion is reported, and so is the reverse
it writes nothing and repairs nothing

grant.note: No tool grant: it is a script the caller runs. It reads the model and the staging tree it is given, writes into a temporary directory it owns, and touches neither the staging tree nor the knowledge root.

failure_outcomes.reason: the model or the staging root does not exist, or the expansion this compares against failed; exit 2, distinguished from a check that ran
the enrichment changed something on the expansion's side of the line, named per object and per field; reported and never repaired

declarations.objective: Move enriched staged objects into the knowledge base, validating each against the base's contract before anything is written. Choose it after the enrichment pass and after the enrichment check. The boundary between staging and the base is a contract change rather than a directory change, and this is where that change is checked. Not for authoring, not for filling a gap, and not for deciding whether an object should exist.

inputs.name: with_open_domain_gaps
inputs.default: absent, and an object whose domain gaps are open is refused: a gap the domain has not closed is a fact the base would be asserting it has

required_context.note: It promotes whatever the expansion staged, so any of the six may pass through it. It reads none of them for meaning: what it checks is conformance.

deterministic_behavior: each object is validated against knowledge-object/5 with its version line substituted, and the substitution is textual so a promotion diff shows a moved file rather than a rewritten one

nothing is written while anything is refused: a partial promotion leaves a base holding some of a run's objects and a staging tree holding the rest, with the edges between them resolving to whichever half a reader looked at
an object carrying an open `kind: domain` gap is refused unless the caller asks otherwise, and the request is reported rather than defaulted
the staged file is removed once its promoted copy is written, and an emptied directory with it
it repairs nothing: an object that fails the contract is named and left where it is

grant.note: No tool grant: it is a script the caller runs. It reads the staging root and writes under the knowledge root, both named by the caller, and reaches nothing else.

failure_outcomes.reason: the staging root does not exist, holds no staged object, or the contract is missing; exit 2, distinguished from a check that ran and refused
one or more objects fail the base's contract, each named with what it lacks; nothing is promoted and the staging tree is untouched
an object still owes the domain a fact, named with what the domain would have to state; the caller may promote it anyway and that decision is recorded

declarations.objective: Write the four fields of one staged knowledge object that no analysis carries — its retrieval question, its one-sentence summary, what it excludes, and the two body sections its node type names — reading the material and the objects around it. Choose it once an expansion has staged a tree and before promotion. Not for deciding what an object is, which the expansion settled from the model; not for closing a gap only the domain can close; and not for editing another object.

required_context.note: It enriches any of the six, and it reads the objects around the one it was given — `out_of_scope` is a claim about the neighbours, so the whole vocabulary is in scope as context even though exactly one object is edited.

deterministic_behavior: exactly one object is edited, the one whose path was given, and no file is created
the fields it may write are a closed list, and a change outside them is found by the boundary check rather than trusted: a tool grant names tools, not the keys of a file
a `kind: domain` gap is left exactly as found — only whoever knows the domain closes one
the `kind: authoring` gap for each field written is removed, because closing it is what records that the field was filled
the result id comes from the caller and is never minted
a disagreement with what the expansion decided is reported as a finding and never edited
judgment: the one question this object answers, and the sentence that summarizes it
what this object does not cover, which is a claim about the objects around it
the two body sections its node type names
whether what the expansion decided is supported by the material, reported and never corrected

grant.note: `Edit` and no `Write`: it changes a file that exists and creates none. The grant cannot confine it to four fields of that file — a grant names tools, not keys — so the confinement is `check-enrichment`, which runs after and compares against a re-derived expansion. No shell.

failure_outcomes.reason: a required input was not supplied, including the result id it never mints

the material does not say what this object is for, so the question it answers cannot be written; blocked with the reason and nothing written, rather than a plausible sentence composed to fill the field
what the expansion decided is not supported by the material; reported as a finding on the result and never edited, and the object is still enriched

declarations.objective: Hold every declared gap to naming a field its node type would actually require, over a staging tree or a knowledge base. Choose it after expansion and before promotion, and over a base whenever its objects change. A gap excuses an object from a field the contract requires, so the excuse is only as good as the field name — and the schema cannot check it, because the requirement a gap excuses is a conditional elsewhere in the same document. Not for validating an object against its contract, which is a boundary check, and not for closing a gap.

required_context.note: What a gap may name depends on the node type, so all six are in scope. It reads no object for meaning.

deterministic_behavior: the fields a node type requires are read from the contract's own per-type conditionals rather than restated, so a second copy cannot fall out of step with the first
a nested alternation counts as a requirement and either side of it may be named: a rule short of both `expression` and `examples` may declare a gap on either
a conditional on `ddd` is resolved against the object at hand, so `identity` is nameable on an entity and not on a value object
`attributes[<name>].<parameter>` is nameable only where the object carries that attribute and its primitive requires that parameter
a `kind: authoring` gap is held to the closed set, derived as the fields the base requires and the staged contract does not
a gap naming a fact the object already declares is reported: a gap records what is missing, and one beside the fact it names keeps an object out of the base for nothing
it writes nothing and repairs nothing

grant.note: No tool grant: it is a script the caller runs. It reads the root it is given and the contract that ships beside it, and writes nothing.

failure_outcomes.reason: the root does not exist, holds no object, or the contract is missing; exit 2, distinguished from a check that ran and found a problem
a gap names a field its node type does not require, or a parameter of an attribute the object does not carry; reported per object and per gap, and never repaired

declarations.objective: Derive the knowledge graph and the three projections from the objects, or verify that the ones on disk are what the objects imply. Choose it after promotion, and again whenever the base changes. Six shipped documents told a consumer these files exist and must never be hand-edited, and nothing produced any of them. Not for authoring, not for validating an object against its contract, and not for repairing a defect it finds.

inputs.name: check
inputs.default: absent, and the derived files are written; with it they are compared and a stale one is reported without being replaced

required_context.note: Every node type becomes a graph node, so all six are in scope. It reads their declared references and none of their prose.

deterministic_behavior: the graph is the objects' declared relationships and nothing inferred: a relationship stated only in prose is not an edge, because two readings of one paragraph produce two graphs
nodes and edges are ordered so identical input produces byte-identical output, and a derived file that reordered between two runs would show a diff nobody caused
the edge vocabulary is the closed table the ontology declares, with each kind's cardinality and whether expansion traverses it
the projections are limited to an index, a glossary and a context map, and the glossary is the set of definitions rather than a list beside them
an edge naming an id the base does not hold is reported as a defect together with orphans, and the graph is still written so a reader sees the shape the defect sits in
a derived file is never read back as an object, so a second run does not grow the graph
it repairs nothing, and under --check it writes nothing at all

grant.note: No tool grant: it is a script the caller runs. It reads the knowledge root it is given and writes four derived files into it, and reaches nothing else.

failure_outcomes.reason: the root does not exist, holds no knowledge object, or holds a file with no frontmatter fence; exit 2, distinguished from a check that ran and found a defect
an edge names an id the base does not hold, or an object is referenced by nothing and references nothing; reported per edge with where in the object it sits, and never repaired

under --check, a derived file on disk is not what the objects imply — it was hand-edited or the objects moved under it; reported and left as found, because regenerating during a check would repair what the check exists to detect
